brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.requirement: Compact desk unit with a drawer
requirements.evidence: Four bases (full at 0,0 / 1,0 / 0,1 and half-e at -1,0) form a compact cluster, locked with joint bolts; check_build meshClash is clear. A drawer frame (notch hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf, ref notch:0#-1,1#notch0) fills the open spot at -1,1 between the bases. Caveat: the standard drawer family (drawer on a half base's cut face) never offered a socket in this build, so the drawer is a notch drawer frame rather than a cut-face drawer, and I did not confirm the drawer's pull-out is clear beyond the mesh check.

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet, to hold a small platform
requirements.evidence: Mount spike spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 sits at the junction where bases 0,0 / 0,1 / 1,0 meet, with platform-sm set as its accessory (setSpikeAccessory succeeded). A solid spike refused the platform (TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED), so the spike was rebuilt as a mount type.

finish.summary: Built a four-base cluster (full bases at 0,0, 1,0, 0,1 plus a half-e at -1,0) with joint bolts, a drawer frame notch at -1,1, and a mount spike at the three-base corner carrying a small platform. check_build reports no errors and meshClash clear. The drawer is a notch-type drawer frame, not the cut-face drawer, because no cut-face drawer socket was ever offered.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
